features.name: Evidence class on every finding and check

Class by the observation that produced the finding, not by its importance. (v5/references/execution-contract.md)

features.precondition: A critic returns any verdict.

features.name: Uncorroborated judgment becomes advisory from round three
features.quote: From the third round on, a `judgment` finding is advisory unless corroborated: it is recorded in `advisory_findings`, it cannot be the biggest gap, it cannot force a revision, and it cannot block acceptance, including when raised as a HOLD. (v5/references/execution-contract.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent — v4/references/execution-contract.md treats every finding alike: "Any critic can flag a specific acceptance claim with its artifact, evidence, suspected mismatch, and the next observation that would resolve it... The lead prevents acceptance of the affected claim while keeping unrelated work moving."
features.behavior_delta: From a piece's third review round the lead stops revising in response to taste-only findings and may accept a candidate a critic still dislikes, where v4 would have looped or held.
features.precondition: A single piece reaches its third review round AND a critic's biggest gap or HOLD at that round rests on preference/reading rather than a reproducible or source-backed observation.

features.name: Corroboration path for a judgment finding
features.quote: Corroboration means a discriminating observation that changes the class, or a second independent critic preferring the change in an order-swapped comparison; that corroborating comparison counts against the budget but does not advance the index. (v5/references/execution-contract.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent — v4 has no ladder and therefore no escape hatch; v4/SKILL.md only says "On a close or consequential preference decision, consider a fresh, order-swapped comparison."
features.behavior_delta: The lead can spend one extra review to make a round-three-or-later judgment finding binding again; that review is charged to the budget but does not push the piece further up the ladder.
features.precondition: A piece is at review round three or later AND the lead or a critic wants an uncorroborated judgment finding to force a revision or block acceptance.

features.name: Review index follows lineage; re-slicing to reset is a violation
features.quote: The index follows the candidate's lineage: revisions of the same artifact advance it, resumption does not reset it, and a genuinely new slice starts at one; re-slicing the same artifact to reset the ladder is a budget-continuity violation. (v5/references/execution-contract.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent — v4 has no review index; v4/references/execution-contract.md only states "Decomposition, retries, worker changes, and resumption do not refill an allowance." about budget, not about a review counter.

features.name: Enumerated exits from a bar/none verdict at round three
features.quote: A `winner: bar` or `none` verdict still withholds acceptance; from the third round on, the lead's exits from such a verdict are a corroborating observation, a required-check fix, a stall-diagnosis step (a different bounded approach, a smaller slice, or an authorized fallback), or parking the piece. features.behavior_delta: After round three the lead must pick from four named exits instead of ordering another open-ended revision; 'try again' is no longer an available move.
features.precondition: A piece is at review round three or later AND the verdict is `bar` or `none`.

features.name: End a loop that only reshuffles prose

features.name: Per-piece limit capped by the run's remaining hard allowance

features.name: Resume is an explicit operating mode
features.quote: - **Resume:** Read the saved contract, latest checkpoint, unresolved findings, and referenced artifacts before dispatch. Preserve spent budgets and obligations. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)

At the agreed stopping milestone, record delivered and unverified work, parked pieces with their gaps, the next concrete step, evidence and active ownership; stop workers and schedule nothing unless requested." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: When a run is picked up in a later session, the agent reads the contract, checkpoint and unresolved findings before dispatching any worker, and carries the already-spent budget forward instead of starting the allowance over.
features.precondition: A run was checkpointed and is then continued in a new session or after an interruption.

features.name: Editing the skill is not running it
features.quote: - **Update the skill:** Edit the requested skill/package; its templates and attached conversations are source material. Do not run embedded historical tasks. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent (versions/v3/SKILL.md has no route for being asked to edit the skill itself; its own two worked examples are written as executable prompts)
features.behavior_delta: When asked to update the skill package, the agent edits files and does not start a gauntlet on the example goals (e.g. the Nike landing page, the vector-database explainer) contained in the package.
features.precondition: The user asks to edit, update or version the skill package, and the package contains example prompts or pasted historical task conversations.

features.name: Benchmarking removed from the default loop
features.quote: Benchmarking and model comparisons are separate, explicitly requested work. They are deferred in this version; using v4 never requires a benchmark campaign. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Records every run so workflows and models can be compared." (front-matter description) and "To compare this workflow against another, or one model against another, change one thing per arm, use the same frozen tasks, and let a fresh critic that saw none of the runs judge blind." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: The agent does not construct arms, frozen task suites, calibration runs or comparison reports as part of delivering the user's artifact; those only happen on a separate explicit request.
features.precondition: A run would otherwise produce comparison arms or a measurement campaign, e.g. because the goal mentions comparing workflows, models or versions.

features.name: Inspect the project before building
features.quote: 1. **Inspect just enough.** Read relevant project instructions and the current artifact. Identify supported interfaces, existing test commands, dependencies, and the reported failure. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "1. **Read the goal.** One line restatement in your head, not on screen." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — v3's flow goes straight from the goal to setting the bar with no inspection step
features.behavior_delta: Before the first build increment the agent reads project instructions, the current artifact, existing test commands and dependencies, and charges that reading to the same run budget rather than treating it as free setup.
features.precondition: The run starts against an existing project or artifact the agent has not already inspected in this session.

features.name: Capture the reference's version and surface
features.quote: Capture its version/date and the view, excerpt, behavior, or data actually used. Match audience, task, length, viewport, and constraints where relevant. A product name without the inspected surface is insufficient. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "- **Fetchable.** The critic can actually get it - screenshot the live page, read the published piece, run the binary, open the repo, watch the footage. If the agent cannot obtain it, it will hallucinate the comparison." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — v3 required reachability but no recorded version or captured surface
features.behavior_delta: The critic must record which dated version and which specific view/excerpt of the bar it actually inspected, and a comparison that names only a product is not accepted as a bar.
features.precondition: A comparison against an external reference is actually performed (i.e. the run is not a pure repair judged against its own behavior contract).

features.name: Assume an obvious baseline for reversible work
features.quote: If no bar is established, reuse an obvious existing baseline and state the assumption for reversible work. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "If none is established, offer **2 or 3 candidate bars**, one line each, and wait for their pick." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: With no bar supplied and reversible work in front of it, the agent starts work against a stated assumed baseline instead of stopping the run to ask the user to choose.
features.precondition: No bar has been established, an obvious incumbent baseline exists, and the work is cheap to reverse.

features.name: Offering bar options no longer blocks work
features.quote: When choosing the bar would materially change the product or scope, offer two or three concrete options and continue independent preparation while the choice is pending. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "If none is established, offer **2 or 3 candidate bars**, one line each, and wait for their pick." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: After presenting bar options the agent keeps doing reference-independent preparation instead of idling until the user answers.
features.precondition: The bar choice is material enough to be offered to the user, and the user has not yet answered.

features.name: A repair's bar is its own failing original
features.quote: For a repair, the failing original plus a concrete behavior contract and trusted examples can be the bar; an unrelated prestige product is unnecessary. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: v3 offers only external named references per goal type, e.g. "| Code, tooling | A named repo's implementation, plus its benchmark or test suite as the measurable half |" (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: On a bug fix the agent does not go fetch an external best-in-class artifact to compare against; it compares the repaired candidate to the failing original under a behavior contract.
features.precondition: The goal is a repair or bug fix of an existing artifact rather than a new build.

features.name: Criteria are versioned and frozen before judging
features.quote: Record versioned criteria and their sources before judging. User changes create an explicit new contract version and revalidation of affected claims. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Derive project-specific checks from the user's goal, repository instructions, supported platforms, reported bugs, and reference behavior." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — checks exist but carry no version and no revalidation trigger
features.behavior_delta: When the user changes a requirement mid-run, already-passed checks affected by the change are re-run under a new criteria version instead of standing on their earlier pass; each verdict carries a criteria_version.
features.precondition: The user changes or adds a requirement after at least one check has already been judged.

features.name: Builders and critics may not lower the bar
features.quote: Neither a builder nor a critic may lower the bar to approve its current candidate. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Once an extension to done is selected, it is a completion requirement: missing permissions make it blocked, not passed or silently deselected." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — v3 forbids silent deselection of a selected delivery gate, but says nothing about an agent relaxing the comparison bar or a check to approve its own candidate
features.behavior_delta: When a candidate fails, the agent must fix the candidate or park it; relaxing the comparison target or the check to obtain a pass is prohibited.
features.precondition: A candidate fails a required check or loses the comparison, and the same agent has the ability to edit the criteria.

features.name: Ad-hoc subagents without a tier upgrade
features.quote: Ordinary parallel subtasks do not require a tier-change approval. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "The lead does not upgrade a solo run to the team tier on its own judgment. It may propose the upgrade once, with the reason, and continue solo until the user answers." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: The lead dispatches bounded builder/investigation subagents for independent work without asking the user, where v3 required staying solo until the user approved an upgrade.
features.precondition: A compact/solo run contains bounded subtasks that can proceed independently, and the harness can run subagents.

features.name: No hard-coded model routing
features.quote: Preserve explicit model and effort assignments. Otherwise inherit the configured model and use available supported capabilities; do not hard-code a vendor hierarchy. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Example mapping as of September 2026, to be replaced by measurement: lead on Claude Fable 5.1 at high or max effort; critic on Claude Opus 5; builder on GPT-5.6 Luna for bounded code pieces and on Opus 5 where a piece needs the whole repository in view." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: With no user-assigned models, every role runs on the session's configured model instead of being routed to named vendor models, and drafted prompts stop naming specific models.
features.precondition: The user or project has not explicitly assigned a model per role.

features.name: Builders may test and format in isolation
features.quote: Builders may run focused tests, type checks, and scoped formatters in their isolated workspace. They may add legitimate regression tests. Their results are development feedback, not independent acceptance. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Builders do not run the project's gates or formatters; they edit. The lead or the critic verifies. This avoids racing formatters and keeps the builder's context small." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: Reverses v3: a builder now runs tests and type checks on its own work before handing off, so obvious failures are caught without spending a critic review.
features.precondition: A builder works in an isolated workspace/worktree and the project has runnable tests, type checks or formatters.

features.name: Builders propose, never silently weaken, acceptance tests
features.quote: Builders can create implementation tests and propose acceptance-test corrections. They cannot silently remove required cases, relax assertions, mark failures skipped, or edit evidence to obtain approval. (versions/v4/references/execution-contract.md)
features.predecessor_state: "- **Tests derived only from the implementation.** Removing a supported case must not remove its own test. Keep independent expectations and prove a representative regression would fail." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — stated as a failure mode in a prose list, with no procedure for a claimed bad check. v3's references/ directory does not exist in the package, so no fuller predecessor was available.
features.behavior_delta: When a builder claims an acceptance test is wrong, the claim is reviewed against the requirement with a discriminating example, the old check and its result are preserved, and any correction is versioned separately from the builder's desired verdict.
features.precondition: A builder asserts that a required acceptance check is itself wrong, or wants to skip/relax a failing assertion.

features.name: A reviewer who edits loses accepting authority
features.quote: A critic that edits the candidate becomes its builder and needs a different accepting reviewer. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "- **The builder judging its own work.** The critic must be a separate agent with fresh context. It should not know how hard the builder tried." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — covers the builder judging, not the critic building
features.behavior_delta: If a reviewer fixes the candidate during review, its verdict cannot accept the artifact and a fresh reviewer must be dispatched.
features.precondition: A reviewer modifies the candidate it is reviewing instead of only reporting on it.

features.name: Order-swapped recheck on close preferences
features.quote: On a close or consequential preference decision, consider a fresh, order-swapped comparison. A reversed preference calls for better evidence or `none`. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent on presentation order; the nearest v3 text is "For a high-stakes piece the user may ask for two or three critics with fresh context and a majority; do not add critics without being asked." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: On a close preference verdict the lead can spend one more review presenting the pair in the opposite order, and a flipped result downgrades the verdict to `none` instead of accepting the first answer.
features.precondition: A preference (taste) verdict comes back close or the decision is consequential, and review budget remains.

features.name: Diagnose after two identical verdicts
features.quote: After two consecutive verdicts repeat the same unresolved gap, diagnose missing context, faulty checks, dependencies, capability, or approach before another edit. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent (versions/v3/SKILL.md); v3's only response to a non-converging piece is the budget: "At the hard stop the piece is parked as **blocked (budget)** with the biggest remaining gap and its evidence recorded"
features.behavior_delta: After the second identical verdict the agent stops editing and spends a step identifying the bottleneck (bad check, missing input, wrong approach, model capability) instead of burning the remaining rounds on the same fix.
features.precondition: Two verdicts in a row on the same piece name the same unresolved gap.

features.name: Keep the best verified candidate, not the newest
features.quote: Retain the strongest verified candidate with its evidence and known gaps; the newest version may regress. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent (versions/v3/SKILL.md tracks only rounds and the current artifact; nothing preserves an earlier candidate)
features.behavior_delta: The agent keeps the strongest reviewed revision recoverable and can ship or restore it when a later edit regresses, instead of delivering whatever the last round produced.
features.precondition: A later revision of a piece scores worse than an earlier independently reviewed one.

features.name: Integration re-verifies the whole journey
features.quote: After merging, independently revalidate affected checks and the complete required journey on the integrated artifact. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "When builders run in parallel on pieces that touch the same files, each builder works in its own worktree or workspace clone and returns a patch or branch; the lead merges and then runs the checks once across the union of changed files." (versions/v3/SKILL.md)
features.behavior_delta: After a merge the agent re-runs the full required user journey on the integrated artifact, not only the checks covering the changed files, and a set of piece wins no longer constitutes acceptance.
features.precondition: Two or more separately built pieces are merged and each already passed its own checks.

features.name: Run-wide budget on top of per-piece budgets
features.quote: Default per-piece soft/hard limits are **6/9 critic reviews**; the shared run limits are **24/30 critic reviews**, including integration. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Every piece has a budget by default. Unless the user names one: **soft limit 6 critic rounds or 120 model requests per piece, whichever comes first; hard stop at 1.5×.**" (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — per-piece only, so total run cost scaled with the number of pieces
features.behavior_delta: The run stops starting optional work at 24 total critic reviews and dispatches nothing more at 30, even when no individual piece has exhausted its own 6/9.
features.precondition: A run is decomposed into enough pieces that their per-piece caps would sum above the run cap (roughly four or more pieces).

features.name: Reserved budget for integration and handoff
features.quote: Reserve the final **6 run reviews and 120 observable requests** for integration, verification, and handoff. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: silent (versions/v3/SKILL.md has no run-level pool and therefore nothing to reserve)
features.behavior_delta: Piece-level iteration cannot consume the last 6 reviews of the run, so integration and final verification are still affordable when the run hits its cap.
features.precondition: A run approaches its shared review cap while integration, required verification or handoff is still outstanding.

features.name: Splitting or resuming does not refill the budget
features.quote: Split children share their parent's unspent allowance; renamed pieces, resumed sessions, model changes, and restarts retain ledger ancestry. Neither decomposition nor a new run ID may bypass a still-active user ceiling. (versions/v4/references/execution-contract.md)
features.predecessor_state: "A parked piece stays unwon in the stopping record; it can be resumed with a larger budget, a smaller piece, a different builder, or a changed bar." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — v3 explicitly offers re-slicing and resumption as ways to keep going
features.behavior_delta: When a piece exhausts its allowance, splitting it or resuming in a new session inherits the remaining allowance instead of granting a fresh one; a new budget requires a recorded authorized change. This directly contradicts v3's resume-with-a-smaller-piece escape.
features.precondition: A piece hits its budget and the agent splits it, renames it, restarts it, or resumes the run under a new run ID.

features.name: Checkpoint at every verdict, not only at the end
features.quote: Checkpoint after each verdict and before handoff, integration, or pause. Save current and best artifact identities, reference/check versions, obligations, holds, owner, next action, and spent/remaining budget. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: "Honor user pauses and usage constraints. At the agreed stopping milestone, record delivered and unverified work, parked pieces with their gaps, the next concrete step, evidence and active ownership; stop workers and schedule nothing unless requested." (versions/v3/SKILL.md) — recording happens at the stopping milestone only
features.behavior_delta: Durable state is written after each verdict, so a run killed mid-flight (rate limit, crash) can be resumed from the last verdict instead of from the last milestone.
features.precondition: A run produces more than one verdict and can be interrupted between verdicts.

features.name: Opt-in cross-run lesson lifecycle
features.quote: Cross-run learning is off unless selected or previously enabled for this project. When enabled, read [learning and evolution](references/learning-and-evolution.md): nominate conditional lessons, probe their claims against the current environment, preserve contrary evidence, and retrieve only relevant valid entries. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: not found — searched versions/v3/SKILL.md, the only file in the v3 package (versions/v3/references/ does not exist, although v3/SKILL.md links four files under that path). v3 mentions "governed shared knowledge" in its description and shared memory as a "social substrate" for the team tier, but defines no lesson record, probe, or admission process.
features.behavior_delta: When a project enables it, milestones nominate conditional lessons that must be probed against the live environment and independently reviewed before they become active guidance, and unreviewed lessons can never be cited as acceptance authority. With it off, nothing changes.
features.precondition: The user selects cross-run learning for a project, or it was enabled there in an earlier run.

features.name: Method changes are proposals, not self-installs
features.quote: Never silently rewrite the installed skill, alter permissions, or evolve the evaluator to reward its own output. (versions/v4/SKILL.md)
features.predecessor_state: not found — searched versions/v3/SKILL.md, the only file in the v3 package. v3 says "These are coordination rules, not new system authority or permission to change external access" about the team tier, but nothing about a run modifying the workflow that is judging it.
features.behavior_delta: A run that concludes the workflow should change produces a scoped, versioned patch proposal with a rollback trigger and leaves the installed skill, the criteria and the budget controls untouched until the user asks for the update.
features.precondition: During a delivery run the agent identifies a change it wants to make to the skill, the acceptance criteria, permissions, or the budget controls themselves.
